title: Sell Mineral Rights in Oliver, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Oliver, PA
metaDescription: Oliver, Fayette County mineral rights owner? We buy oil and gas interests near old coal-patch land, explain the paperwork, and pay a fair cash price.
heroLead: Oliver is a small community in Fayette County built up around old coal-patch land, and mineral ownership here often reflects that history — surface and subsurface rights split apart generations ago by coal companies that came through long before Marcellus shale was ever on anyone's radar.
intro: Fayette County patch towns like Oliver have some of the most tangled title histories we deal with anywhere in the state. A family might hold the surface, someone else might hold the coal from a reservation filed in the early 1900s, and the oil and gas rights might have followed a completely separate path through inheritance. Sorting that out is exactly the kind of work we do before we ever put a number in front of you.

sections.heading: Patch-Town Title Work Takes Patience
paragraphs: We start by pulling every recorded instrument touching your Oliver tract from the Fayette County recorder of deeds in Uniontown, tracing coal, oil, and gas severances separately since they don't always move together. It's not unusual to find that a family assumed they'd lost all mineral rights decades ago when in fact only the coal was severed, leaving oil and gas rights intact and available to sell or lease today.

Once we've confirmed exactly what you hold, we look at how close your tract sits to current Marcellus activity on the southern edge of the wet-gas fairway, since that proximity drives most of the value in this part of Fayette County.

sections.heading: Why Some Families Choose to Sell Here
paragraphs: For owners holding a small fractional interest that's been passed down through several generations of a patch-town family, managing that interest — tracking lease renewals, disputing deduction line items, chasing down co-heirs for a future sale — can feel like more trouble than it's worth for a modest royalty. Selling outright ends that upkeep in one transaction.

faqs.question: My family only owns the surface in Oliver, not the coal. Do we still have oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Possibly. Coal, oil, and gas are often severed separately, so losing coal rights doesn't necessarily mean you lost oil and gas rights too. We check the full chain of title to confirm.

faqs.question: How do I know if my interest has ever been leased?
faqs.answer: We search the Fayette County lease records as part of our free review and let you know what we find.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum interest size you'll buy?
faqs.answer: No, we buy fractional interests of any size, including very small legacy shares.
